**CHARGE NUMBER:** 1901
**PROJECT TITLE:** Biochemical Modification of Tobacco
**PERIOD COVERED:** May 1-31, 1979
**PROJECT LEADER:** D. M. Teng
**DATE OF REPORT:** June 8, 1979

## I. <u>CONTROLLED FERMENTATION-DENITRIFICATION</u>

### A. <u>Pilot Plant Facility</u><sup>1</sup>

The continuous centrifuge system was tested by New Brunswick Scientific Company personnel and found to be functioning satisfactorily. Three 50-liter autoclavable containers were modified into an inoculum retention and transfer unit. Application of a vacuum at the air inlet facilitated the transfer of inoculum from the retention tanks into the 500-liter fermenter through the drain. After satisfactory test of all systems in the 500-liter fermenter, experiments were conducted to access the effect of retaining the inoculum in the retaining tank at room temperature before inoculation. No adverse effect in denitrification was noticed.

### B. <u>Pilot Denitrification Test</u><sup>2</sup>

An initial pilot denitrification of SEL in the 500-liter fermenter was accomplished. The inoculum buildup was accomplished by growing the starter in the 28-liter fermenters and then in the 500-liter fermenter. The inoculum was retained in the retention tanks during the autoclaving of SEL and necessary components in the 500-liter fermenter. After cooling, the inoculum was introduced into the SEL. Denitrification was accomplished in 20 hours. All the controls and inoculum-transferring system functioned satisfactorily.

As the bulk quantity chemicals needed for our pilot runs were damaged during shipment, further testing must be delayed until the chemicals are received.

### C. <u>Pilot Supporting Laboratory</u>

The laboratory in "C" Pilot Plant is now operational and experiments to define optimal scale-up inoculum have been designed and are in progress.

## II. <u>CONTROLLED FERMENTATION-CELLULASE</u>

### A. <u>Scale-up of <u>Trichoderma viride</u> Cellulase</u><sup>3</sup>

A portion of the pH profile of *T. viride* cellulase production in a shake flask was determined. The whole profile will be determined within the next couple of weeks.
